title: Precision Handoff Scheduler with Profiled Validation
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement a runtime scheduler that selects and dispatches execution kernels across mixed-precision paths (FP16 / FP8 / INT8) using persistent per-model quantization profiles, lightweight on-request calibration signals, and a profile-driven accuracy validation step before committing to lower precision for a given request bulk. The goal is to reduce per-token cost without violating customer quality SLOs by: 1) attaching a compact quant profile to model artifacts that includes per-layer expected activation ranges, observed dynamic ranges, and a conservative accuracy delta estimate; 2) running a fast input-distribution estimator at request time to match batch characteristics to stored profiles; 3) selecting a candidate precision path (e.g., hybrid FP16/FP8) and performing a micro-validation sampling harness (sample < 1% tokens or a short prefix) to verify calibrated output quality; 4) committing the full request to chosen kernels or falling back to the safer FP16 path. This ticket focuses on the scheduler, kernel registry integration, sampling-driven validation, telemetry hooks, and a safe swap protocol to avoid visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can select and route requests to FP16, FP8, INT8 kernel paths via the kernel registry based on model profile + input estimator
Micro-validation harness runs within bounded latency (tail + median budget defined) and produces pass/fail for path commit
Safe swap protocol implemented: when validation fails, request falls back to FP16 without double-charging customers and with audit log entries
Telemetry emitted: per-request chosen path, validation result, delta metrics (latency, token-cost), sampled accuracy signals
Performance regression <3% p50 latency and cost savings >= 12% on targeted quantizable models in synthetic workload benchmark
decisions: Use stored quant profiles shipped with model bundle (profile schema v2) rather than probing full calibration at runtime
Micro-validation will sample short prefixes and compare deterministic evaluation metrics (logprob delta + structured output checks) rather than full human eval
Fallback hierarchy: INT8 -> FP8 -> FP16; avoid fallback to mixed INT8+FP8 path until stable calibration telemetry is available
Initial rollout gated to internal canary customers and internal test workloads before public release

notes: Tradeoffs: full calibration at load time yields stronger guarantees but increases startup cost and complicates Private/VPC deployments. Chosen approach biases to conservative stored profiles + fast runtime checks.
Telemetry: add 'validation_outcome' tag (pass|fail|timeout) and 'profile_match_score' (0..1) to existing request traces. Expose aggregated per-model histogram in Console.
Safety: include explainability hooks (sampled input, sampled golden-output) for failures so SRE/Customer Success can investigate regressions.
Next steps: wire rollout flags, implement dashboard in Console (runtime-1.22), run canary for 2 weeks, gather user-level quality signals and cost savings report.
